title.narrative: Child Labour and its worst forms eliminated

description.narrative:
Sri Lanka has strengthened its legal, institutional, and operational frameworks to eliminate forced labour and child labour, in line with its obligations under ILO Conventions No. 29 and No. 105 and the Protocol of 2014. Forced labour is now explicitly criminalized in national legislation, with reinforced prevention and enforcement measures, particularly in foreign employment through tighter regulation of recruitment agencies, mandatory worker registration, and improved detection of human trafficking.
At the national level, Sri Lanka has demonstrated sustained commitment through its engagement as an Alliance 8.7 Pathfinder Country, the establishment of a Government Task Force on Forced Labour, and the adoption of a national Action Plan to implement Protocol 29. With technical assistance from the ILO, capacity-building initiatives are strengthening law enforcement and labour administration to improve identification, enforcement, and coordinated responses to forced and child labour, including their worst forms, while underscoring the need to address remaining risks within domestic labour markets.
